findings.title: SQL injection via f-string in search_orders_advanced
findings.explanation: search_orders_advanced builds SQL with f"... LIKE '%{query}%'" allowing attacker-controlled q to break out of string literal and inject arbitrary SQL, read/modify data.

evidence.why: User-controlled query interpolated directly into SQL via f-string, no parameterization.

findings.suggestion: Use parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT ... WHERE status LIKE ?", (f"%{query}%",))

findings.title: Unauthenticated endpoint exposes all users' orders
findings.explanation: orders_search2 exposes search_orders_advanced without authentication or per-user scoping, unlike orders_search. Any caller can enumerate all users' orders, IDs, totals and statuses.

evidence.why: New endpoint takes only q with no User auth and returns all orders.
Docstring says power search across all users orders, no user scoping.

findings.suggestion: Require authenticated User and scope query to that user like search_orders does, or remove endpoint.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS key in shop/uploads.py
findings.explanation: RECEIPT_AWS_KEY is hardcoded in shop/uploads.py. Secrets in source leak via VCS, logs, and builds. Should be loaded from environment or secret manager.

evidence.why: AWS key hardcoded in source file, committed to version control.

findings.suggestion: Remove hardcoded key; load from environment variable or secret manager and never commit secrets.
